- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward → reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward → cap forecast decline or add 1–2% upward adjustment.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.2), model frequently underestimates upward momentum → increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model tends to lag mean reversion by 2–4 days → adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true values if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- When sentiment is strongly negative and price is falling, model often underpredicts the drop → increase downward forecast slope by 0.3–0.7% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early days (1–7) and underestimates late days (25–30) → apply upward bias to first 3 days and downward bias to last 3 days if sentiment is negative.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often fails to capture momentum → add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast for next 5 days.
- Model underestimates true volatility when sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or higher) → increase forecast spread by 0.2–0.5% for 3–7 day horizon.
